accuracy.evidence: Checked against NSIDC 'Glacier quick facts' and 'Science of glaciers': snow that survives a melt season becomes firn, about two thirds as dense as water; burial squeezes out air until it is glacier ice, which for most glaciers takes more than a hundred years (kid text and lab DONE line); glaciers flow down and out under their own weight; growth or shrinkage depends on snow gained against ice lost (NSIDC mass balance). NSIDC 'Ice sheet quick facts': Greenland about 7.4 m and Antarctica about 58 m of sea level (lab gauge, m5, kid text; key idea's 'about 65 m' is 7.4 + 58). NSIDC Arctic sea ice facts: floating sea ice does not directly raise sea level (step 4 and m4). Abrasion, plucking, U-shaped valleys and moraine follow the British Geological Survey and Geological Society glacial landform pages. EPICA Dome C reaches about 800,000 years; ice-age CO2 about 180-190 ppm, pre-1800 about 280 ppm, NOAA over 420 ppm today. The lab says the drawings are not to scale (art file note), and the 10-years run is a model, not real rates. Parameterised answers a*10, a-b (a 6-10, b 1-5; a 8-12, b 2-7, always positive) and a*b checked at the corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented geography slips: glacier as a frozen river or lake (Snow to ice predict, challenge 'river', p1); cold alone makes a glacier (summer-melt feedback 'Ice only builds up where more snow falls in winter than melts in summer', challenge 'cold', m2); a retreating glacier flows backwards (Grow or shrink predict 'Back up the valley', the stone that keeps moving downhill while the end retreats, challenge 'back', p3); river V and glacial U confused (Carving predict 'The same V', V-shape feedback, challenge 'vee', p5); melting sea ice floods coasts (Ice and the sea predict 'Rises a lot', sea-ice feedback, sorter, challenge 'sea', m4); Greenland holds most ice (challenge 'size', m5); deeper ice is younger (core ordering feedback 'The top ice is the newest', challenge 'young', m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagglacier models glacier mechanisms that no other lab has: a yearly snow stack whose layers turn from snow to firn to glacier ice as more winters are added; a mass-balance model with snow and melt bars that moves the snout while a stone on the ice always travels downhill; a valley cross-section that morphs from V to U as the glacier is dragged in, leaving moraine; a sea-level gauge filled by melting sea ice, Greenland and Antarctica; and an ice-sheet section drilled for samples that are ordered by age. The tundra, polar exploration and rock cycle labs deal with ecosystems, history and rock types, not ice formation, flow, erosion or sea level. The lab_distinct gate measures it under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is found by doing it before the text confirms it: the learner adds winters and watches their first snow become firn and then ice; dragging the summer sun removes the newest layer, showing why snow must outlast the summer; in Grow or shrink they must set snow above, below and equal to melt to meet each goal, and see the end retreat while the stone moves down; dragging the glacier into the valley three times widens the V into a U; melting each kind of ice shows the gauge barely move for sea ice and jump for the ice sheets; drilling three depths and ordering them shows deeper means older.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the lab then disproves: 'A frozen river or lake' (the stack is built only from snow); 'Back up the valley' (the stone keeps moving downhill as the end retreats); 'The same V' (the carved section becomes a U); 'Rises a lot' for sea ice (the gauge stays at +0 m when the sea ice melts). A.reveal adds 'now you know why' to each completed task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions rotate answer order; each wrong option maps to a named slip with its own message: 'river' (snow squeezed into ice, not frozen water), 'back' (ice melts at the end faster than it arrives; it still flows downhill), 'sea' (sea ice already floats; only land ice adds water), 'vee' (rivers cut V, glaciers leave U), 'young' (snow piles on top, so deeper ice is older), 'size' (Greenland about 7 m, Antarctica about 58 m), 'land' (land ice runs into the sea when it melts), 'cold' (cold is not enough without snow). In-lab wrong moves also get specific feedback (wrong mass balance names which side won, the V answer, the wrong core order).

readability.evidence: Kid explanation Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.9 and adult 9.3, within the learner limits (6.5 and 9.5). Kid paragraphs use short sentences and define each new word as it comes (firn 'looks like wet sugar', moraine 'piles of rock', ice sheets 'glaciers as big as countries'). Lab banners are one or two short sentences; feedback lines stay within four lines on a 390 px phone.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph carries one mechanism (formation, flow and balance, erosion, ice sheets and cores); adult paragraphs give curriculum placement and key words, sourced facts, common mistakes, and what the lab does. No filler phrases; the content gate passed. The family tip is a concrete activity (look at a valley photo, freeze coloured layers).

mobile.evidence: Checked on screenshots at 390 px in light and dark themes (before, mid and after each task): the snow stack, the snow and melt bars with the Run pill, the valley section with the U and V pills, the sea gauge with three ice cards, and the ice core with sample pills all fit without clipping. Feedback lines wrap inside the canvas; buttons below the canvas are full-size tap targets. The first version clipped the core feedback and drew a thin glacier on a steep slope; both were fixed and re-checked.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: add a winter or a warm summer, snow and melt plus and minus with Run 10 years, push the glacier and U or V, melt each kind of ice, drill each depth and order the samples. The canvas aria-label updates with every change and c.say announces it. The browser gate's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors.
